title: Noise-Robust Density Estimation for Tabular Data Anomaly Detection
topic: General Machine Learning->Unsupervised and Semi-supervised Learning
claim: Existing detectors confuse benign noise-induced shifts with true anomalies; ours keeps noisy normal data separate from anomalies.
layout: 6 scatter panels in 2x3 grid, shared legend, AUROC in captions
description: A 2x3 grid of scatter plots. Each plot shows anomaly score on the y-axis against sample index (0 to 3000) on the x-axis. The samples are grouped into three blocks of 1000: green points for normal data, blue for noisy normal data, and red for anomalous data. Panels (a) to (e) show kNN, KDE, LOF, DSVDD and RealNVP. In these panels the blue block sits high, at about the same level as the red block or above the green block. This means noisy normal samples are scored as anomalies. Panel (f), NRDE (ours, in bold), keeps the green and blue blocks at the same low level and lifts only the red block. Captions give AUROC values, rising from 59.2 to 83.3 for NRDE. The legend sits in the top-left panel. The eye goes to the last panel, where the red block clearly separates from the rest.
caption: Detection performance on a synthetic dataset. A larger anomaly score indicates that the sample is more likely to be anomalous. The data were generated from a few data sources and many noise sources. Points marked in green, blue, and red represent normal data, noisy normal data (caused by noise change), and anomalous data, respectively. See (8) for definitions. The five compared methods detect most of the noisy normal samples as anomalies, while our NRDE is robust to changes in noise. More details about this experiment are in Appendix F.
abstract: Density-based anomaly detection methods often provide accurate and interpretable predictions but their performance can be severely degraded by the inherent noise of data, such as changes arising from environmental conditions during data collection or background noise. To deal with such noise, we present noise-robust density estimation (NRDE) for tabular data anomaly detection. We aim to estimate the density of pure data with the influence of noises isolated, which is a non-trivial task since the data-generating process is completely unknown. Specifically, NRDE learns a Jacobian-regularized normalizing flow to estimate the sources of data and categorizes sources into two groups, where one group generates pure data and the other generates noise. After generating pure data, we can use the density of such pure data to detect anomalies caused by the sources of pure data solely. Therefore, NRDE is robust to inherent noise. We provide theoretical results to support the effectiveness of NRDE and compare NRDE with $17$ baselines on $47$ benchmark datasets under different settings, including vanilla anomaly detection, anomaly detection with anomaly contamination, anomaly detection on noisy data, and transductive outlier detection.
